output_variables.flag_cli_cannot_cite_a_local_note: sase flag (phase sase-nb.7), its three doctor checks, and the FlagTriage gate text ship globally and run from any project, but sase/memory/sase_flags.md will now exist only in the sase repo. Any user-facing string that tells the reader to read that path must either drop it or resolve it and mention it only when present. Open question the correction surfaces: the flag registry lives in sase's own source, so 'sase flag new' run from another project would file a flag bead in that project's store for a registry it cannot edit. Consider gating sase flag new on the is_sase_managed marker (project_management.py:15) or warning outside a sase-managed repo.
output_variables.formatting_is_now_manual: Generated notes are auto-formatted by format_generated_memory_markdown and validated at render time (description required, frontmatter applied by apply_memory_frontmatter). A hand-written sase/memory/sase_flags.md gets none of that: the author must hand-write the frontmatter, fold the description to the repo's line width, and satisfy the ordinary markdown lint gate in just check. Copy the shape of sase/memory/symvision.md rather than writing frontmatter from scratch.
output_variables.glossary_and_docs_stay_where_they_are: Do not over-apply the correction. (1) The glossary addition is already project-local: memory.glossary in this repo's sase/sase.yml renders sase/memory/glossary.md per project (init_memory/glossary.py docstring: 'Project-local glossary memory generation'), so Feature Flag and Flag Bead need no change. (2) docs/configuration.md's feature-flag section still serves every project, because scope:'project' flags are overridable from any project's local sase.yml (plan line 347). Local memory does not imply a local config surface — only the teaching note and the Tier 1 pointer move.
output_variables.tier1_pointer_is_the_same_bug: The plan's always-loaded Feature Flags pointer is planned for src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase.template.md, which renders sase/memory/sase.md into EVERY sase project. That is the same generated-vs-local mistake with a larger blast radius: it would put 'run sase flag new' into the always-loaded Tier 1 context of projects that cannot own a flag. Fix: put the pointer in a project-local Tier 1 short note in this repo (its own type:short, parent:AGENTS.md note, or a section in sase/memory/gotchas.md). Side effect: the plan's 90-word Tier 1 budget was priced as text loaded in every project; loaded only in sase, the budget can be relaxed if the guidance needs it.
output_variables.verification_shift: Phase sase-nb.10's exit condition 'sase init -c reports no memory drift' stops covering sase_flags.md, because drift checks compare generated files against their templates and a hand-written note has no template. Replace it with three checks: sase memory list shows sase_flags.md as a Tier 2 note with its description; the regenerated AGENTS.md Tier 2 listing includes it; and sase init in a non-sase project produces NO sase_flags.md (the inverse check that proves the correction actually took). A local long note is auto-indexed only if its frontmatter carries parent: AGENTS.md — inventory_reachability.py blocks a long note whose parent target does not exist.
